study_identification_part.si_4_title: Toward Understanding Autism Heterogeneity: Identifying Clinical Subgroups and Neuroanatomical Deviations

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Warped likelihood Bayesian Linear Regression implemented in PCNtoolkit (Version 0.26) in Python.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Here, we performed normative modeling on CT and subcortical regions of interests (ROIs) using warped likelihood Bayesian Linear Regression (Fraza et al., 2021) model implemented in the PCNtoolkit (Version 0.26) in Python (Version 3.9.16).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Meijer2024.pdf.md: Normative modeling / paragraph starting "Here, we performed normative modeling"

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness (CT) and subcortical volumes (subcortical ROIs).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Normative modeling is a novel statistical framework that allows to compare individual-level neuroanatomical features (CT and subcortical volume) to a reference population (Marquand et al., 2016, 2019; Rutherford et al., 2022, 2023).
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Meijer2024.pdf.md: Normative modeling / paragraph starting "Normative modeling is a novel statistical framework"

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Covariates: age, site, FIQ, Euler number (quality measure), and intracranial volume for subcortical volumes.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We included age, site, FIQ, and quality measures (i.e., the Euler number) as covariates and additional intracranial volume for subcortical volumes.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Meijer2024.pdf.md: Normative modeling / paragraph starting "Here, we performed normative modeling"
